label: Early original-phase steps shortly after an "a" in the first three positions
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at steps t=2..5, 1-3 steps after the letter a appeared at one of positions 0-2. The input token at the firing step itself does not matter. prev2_tok=a has 15x lift and first_tok=a has 8.8x lift. The strongest activations come from sequences that start with a run of a (e.g. a a a ...): there the feature peaks at t=3-4 and then fades over the next 2-3 steps. When a is later in the sequence (position >= 3) the activation is weak or absent, and steps after a later a make up most of the low-quartile misses. It never fires at t=0 or t=1, never in the copy phase, and only rarely at the delimiter (1% of mass). Activation goes down as the sequence has more digits. Main false positives are the edges of the window, where the activation has already decayed to zero.

issues: The main factual claims hold. On the dev split the feature never fires at t=0 or t=1 (0 of 1M steps) and never in the copy phase (0 active). The delimiter holds 1.0% of the activation mass. Mass by t is 0.27/0.43/0.23/0.07 for t=2..5, so it peaks at t=3-4. prev2_tok=a has 15.2x lift and first_tok=a has 8.8x lift. Precision falls steadily with n_digits (0.81, 0.76, 0.72, 0.68, 0.60 for 0-4 digits).
With no a anywhere in the sequence, firing is almost nil: F1 0.004, mass recall 0.002, all of it in the lowest activation quartile. So 'a' really is the trigger.

Small systematic gap: an a at position 3 does fire at t=4 (precision 0.51, about 5% of active steps). The explanation says activation is 'weak or absent' when a is at position 3 or later, and the label says 'first three positions', so both slightly understate this. An a at position 1 also fires at t=5 (precision 0.51), which the predicate's t<=4 cutoff leaves out.
Small systematic false-positive class: phase<=1 lets in the delimiter step when L=4 (t=4), where precision is only 0.205. Restricting to phase==0 removes it.

Over-firing at orig(0)=a, t=4 (precision 0.44) is explained by the repeated-a pattern. With 2 or more a's seen, precision is 0.98; with a single a it is 0.38. This fits the explanation's point that runs of a ('a a a ...') give the strongest activations.

Refined predicate: test F1 0.832 vs 0.805 reported (P 0.772, R 0.902, mass recall 0.968). It is the same concept with corrected window edges, not a different feature, so the label and explanation stand with a minor positional correction.
